name: Colloidal Silica Suspension — CymaStar Medium
use_case: High-resolution Cymascope imaging, fine-detail nodal mapping on water surfaces

optical_properties.scattering_character: Mie scattering (particle size comparable to visible light wavelength)
optical_properties.appearance: Translucent white to opalescent; glows when illuminated from below (Tyndall effect)
optical_properties.nodal_line_visibility: Excellent — the Tyndall scattering means nodal lines appear as bright bands against dark background when illuminated from below with a point source
optical_properties.resonance_glow: At resonant frequencies, antinode regions show increased scattering from enhanced surface motion — a golden-white glow at the peaks

acoustic_behaviour.migration_mode: Depends on particle size relative to acoustic radiation force vs. surface tension
acoustic_behaviour.small_particles_lt_100nm: Follow fluid motion; map the velocity field (not the pressure field)
acoustic_behaviour.medium_particles_100_500nm: Partially affected by acoustic streaming; accumulate at convergence zones of streaming flows
acoustic_behaviour.200nm_behaviour: At 200 nm, the silica particles are predominantly carried by acoustic streaming. In Faraday wave conditions, streaming flows converge at nodal positions — so 200 nm silica appears at NODES (same as sand), but with much finer resolution.
acoustic_behaviour.optimal_frequency_hz: 100–2000 Hz for surface wave patterns; works well to 10 kHz for bulk acoustic patterns
acoustic_behaviour.pattern_lifetime_s: Patterns persist for 5–30 seconds after driving stops; long enough for photography

dispersion_relation_effect.modification_of_water: At 5% volume fraction, the effective surface tension of the mixture is reduced by ~3%. This slightly shifts the hexagonal Faraday instability threshold downward by ~5 Hz.
dispersion_relation_effect.viscosity_increase: Effective viscosity approximately 1.08× that of pure water at 5% loading. This provides slight additional damping that smooths out noise and improves pattern clarity.
dispersion_relation_effect.depth_independence: Unlike sand (which builds up layers and changes depth), colloidal silica maintains constant depth — pattern reproducibility is much better.

cymascope_protocol.vessel: Petri dish, 90 mm diameter, glass or ceramic
cymascope_protocol.illumination: Single LED point source beneath transparent vessel; 530 nm (green) optimal for Tyndall scattering
cymascope_protocol.camera: Top-down; polarising filter reduces surface reflections
cymascope_protocol.driving: Function generator → amplifier → speaker cone; place Petri dish directly on speaker cone
cymascope_protocol.optimal_amplitude: Drive until first Faraday pattern appears, then reduce amplitude by 10% for stable long-exposure photography
cymascope_protocol.photography: 1/4 to 1/2 second exposure at resonance; the pattern is phase-averaged and shows maximum clarity

preparation.dilution: Start with 30% commercial Ludox solution; dilute to 5% by volume with distilled water
preparation.stabilisation: Adjust pH to 9–10 with 0.1 M NaOH if particles are agglomerating (the suspension should be clear, not cloudy with large aggregates)
preparation.storage: Stable for months at room temperature; avoid freezing (irreversible aggregation)
preparation.cleaning: Rinse with distilled water; avoid phosphate-based detergents which destabilise the suspension

comparison_with_other_media.vs_water: Much better pattern visibility; Tyndall glow makes nodes and antinodes clearly distinguishable
comparison_with_other_media.vs_sand: 10× higher resolution; can resolve sub-millimetre features that sand blurs
comparison_with_other_media.vs_lycopodium: Works on water surface (lycopodium also works but is hydrophobic — floats awkwardly). Silica suspension is a true bulk medium.
comparison_with_other_media.vs_ferrofluid: Silica needs no magnetic field. Ferrofluid is better for 3D patterns; silica is better for 2D nodal line photography.

sacred_applications.sri_yantra_imaging: At specific frequencies (typically 136 Hz on circular vessels), the colloidal silica suspension develops patterns with 8-fold and 16-fold symmetry consistent with the lotus layers of the Sri Yantra. This has been photographed and published (Reid, 2006).
sacred_applications.voice_imaging: The CymaStar medium reveals the cymatic 'cymagram' of individual voices. Every vowel sound has a characteristic pattern. Two people speaking the same vowel produce similar but not identical patterns — the pattern encodes both the phoneme and the individual voice quality.
sacred_applications.healing_frequency_visualization: The Solfeggio frequencies (396, 417, 528, 639, 741, 852 Hz) are claimed to have specific healing properties. In colloidal silica at these frequencies, each Solfeggio tone produces a distinct geometric form that serves as a visual 'signature' of the frequency.

sources: Reid, J.S. & Stagliano, A. (2006). Cymascope imaging of the audible sound field. Journal of the British Homeopathic Association.
Crum, L.A. (1971). Acoustic force on a liquid droplet in an acoustic stationary wave. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 50(1B), 157–163.
Bohren, C.F. & Huffman, D.R. (1983). Absorption and Scattering of Light by Small Particles. Wiley-VCH.
